published_statement: Abstract p.1: 'We present the first direct measurement of the frequency ratio of these two clock transitions, without reference to a cesium primary standard, and using the same single ion of 171Yb+. The absolute frequencies of both transitions are also presented, each with a relative standard uncertainty of 6 x 10^-16. Combining our results with those from other experiments, we report a three-fold improvement in the constraint on the time-variation of the proton-to-electron mass ratio, mu-dot/mu = 0.2(1.1) x 10^-16 year^-1, along with an improved constraint on time-variation of the fine structure constant, alpha-dot/alpha = -0.7(2.1) x 10^-17 year^-1.' p.1: 'the first direct measurement of the ratio between the E3 and E2 optical transition frequencies in 171Yb+, with fractional uncertainty 3 x 10^-16.' p.1: 'The absolute frequencies of both the E3 and E2 transitions have been measured with increasingly high accuracy and are now limited by Cs primary standards.' p.3: 'nu_E3/nu_E2 = 0.932 829 404 530 964 65(31)'; Table I TOTAL sigma/nu0: E2 6.13, E3 5.79, ratio 3.36 (x1e-16); 'a statistical relative standard uncertainty on the mean ratio of 7 x 10^-17, and 5 x 10^-16 on each of the absolute frequencies'. p.4: 'Time variation of alpha and mu is measured via the frequency ratio of two clock transitions r = nu_1/nu_2 using the relation r-dot/r = (A_1 - A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1 - B_2) mu-dot/mu. The sensitivity coefficients A_i of the relevant atomic transitions are: A_E3 = -5.95 [34], A_E2 = 0.88 [35], and A_Cs = 2.83 [36]. Dependence on mu-dot arises through the nuclear magnetic moment and is negligible for optical transitions (the sensitivity coefficient B_E3 = B_E2 = 0). As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu (B_Cs = -1).' p.4: mu = m_p/m_e; constraints 'on the assumption of local position invariance and that any time-variation is linear'.
published_hypotheses: H-LIN: the linear-response relation r-dot/r = (A_1-A_2) alpha-dot/alpha + (B_1-B_2) mu-dot/mu (p.4), i.e. frequencies depend on the constants only through power laws alpha^A mu^B at fixed other quantities.

H-AOPT: A_E3 = -5.95, A_E2 = 0.88, A_Cs = 2.83 are atomic-structure calculations taken from refs [34]-[36] (Dzuba-Flambaum 2008; Dzuba-Flambaum-Marchenko 2003; Dzuba-Flambaum-Webb 1999), not measured here.
H-BOPT: B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 because mu-dependence of an optical transition (through the nuclear magnetic moment) is 'negligible' (p.4) -- an approximation, not an identity.
H-GCS: B_Cs = -1 rests on 'the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38]' (p.4, Flambaum-Tedesco 2006; Berengut-Flambaum-Kava 2011).
H-LPI: the mu-dot and alpha-dot constraints assume 'local position invariance and that any time-variation is linear' (p.4).

H-BUDGET: the 3e-16 and 6e-16 are Table I totals (3.36, 6.13, 5.79 x1e-16) from the listed systematics plus statistics over 105 h (E2) and 81 h (E3), Feb-Mar 2014, with extrapolation of observed instabilities to the whole period (p.3); the absolute totals are dominated by the Cs-referenced statistical term (4.77, 5.35) and include Cs fountain systematics 1.90 (Table II).
hypothesis_drift: DROPPED H-GCS (the source's condition for B_Cs = -1): the tree's verbatim quote at address.py:436-440 elides, with '...', exactly the sentence 'As the 133Cs nuclear g-factor has negligible sensitivity to changes in the strong interaction [37, 38], an AFM history can also be interpreted to set constraints on mu-dot/mu' before '(B_Cs = -1)'. The tree's model nu_hf ~ alpha^2 g_I (m_e/m_p) F_rel (address.py:62, 615, 1243) holds g_I fixed without naming that as a hypothesis, and CONTROL 1 (address.py:1241-1252) 'derives' B_Cs = -1 from that same fixed-g_I model, so the control is consistent with, not independent of, H-GCS. The drop matters in the tree's setting specifically: a displaced vev moves X_q = m_q/Lambda_QCD at d ln X_q/d ln v = 7/9 (H1) or 1 (H2) (address.py:283), which is exactly the strong-interaction change H-GCS assumes negligible. COMPUTED (rederive G) with a Cs exponent kappa_q = +/-0.009 (a web-search snippet of physics/0309107, NOT READ): the optical/Cs eps_det moves by <= 1% from this term alone; no verdict moves.

WEAKENED-BY-OMISSION (the tree's own model, not a quote error): address.py:625-628 ratio_sensitivity uses 'B and K only', i.e. drops the source's (A_1 - A_2) alpha term of H-LIN from the optical/Cs channel. Under H2 K_alpha = 0 exactly, so nothing is lost; under H1 K_alpha = +1.8497e-3 and COMPUTED (rederive G) the E3/Cs sensitivity becomes -0.7473 instead of -0.7311 (eps_det 8.03e-16 vs the tree's 8.21e-16, 2.2%); E2/Cs 0.5%. The docstring states 'using B and K only', so the omission is visible, but it is not named as a hypothesis at the eps_det_stationary site (address.py:828-831).

NUANCE, not drift: the tree calls the 6e-16 'Cs-limited' (address.py:67, 115-117, 829). The source supports it (p.1 'now limited by Cs primary standards'), but the budget (Table I/II) shows the limit is the Cs-referenced STATISTICS (4.77 / 5.35 of 6.13 / 5.79, i.e. 61% / 85% of the variance), not the Cs fountain systematics (1.90, ~10%). That the absolute statistics come from the Cs reference chain is an inference from the ratio's statistical 0.68 on the same ion and run (>= 98% of the absolute statistical variance is not optical noise, rederive D) -- labelled as inference.

ROUNDING, a discrepancy not an error: CS_CHANNEL_COARSER_BY = 6e-16/3e-16 = 2 'COMPUTED' (address.py:68, 880) divides two figures the source printed to one significant digit. From Table I the factor is 6.13/3.36 = 1.82 (E2) and 5.79/3.36 = 1.72 (E3); from the printed digits 1.84 and 1.73. The W10 correction it supports ('2, not 100') stands at every reading.

SCOPE (not a drift in the tree's use): H-LPI and linear drift attach to the source's mu-dot / alpha-dot constraints, which the tree does not use; the tree uses only the coefficients (partial derivatives from atomic theory) and the measurement uncertainties. Using them for a spatially displaced vev (address.py section 7) needs the coefficients, not LPI.

SCOPE: the tree uses GODUN_ABS_UNC (a 72-105 h time-averaged absolute-frequency uncertainty against NPL-CsF2) as 'the fractional accuracy of an optical-to-Cs ratio' for detecting eps (address.py:115-117, 828-831). This is a representative scale, correctly labelled as Godun's; the tree does not claim it is an achievable accuracy for a spatial comparison, and the tree's section 7 separately names better channels.

PRESERVED: mu = m_p/m_e (address.py:440); B_E3 = B_E2 = 0 carried as 'negligible, not zero' (address.py:41-43) and the tree's own W10 computes a nonzero same-place optical term; the three A values, two B values and two uncertainties equal the printed ones exactly (rederive G).

lacked_data: What the authors had: their own Feb-Mar 2014 data (E2 105 h, E3 81 h, 72 h overlap) against NPL-CsF2, the AFM histories of NPL/PTB and five other species, and theoretical coefficients from 1999-2008 atomic-structure calculations and 2006-2011 nuclear-g-factor estimates. What came later: (i) the same ratio at 3.4e-18 (Lange 2021, NOT READ) -- its central value sits 2.3 sigma from Godun's, which is consistent with Godun's budget being somewhat optimistic (the leading term was the E2 residual quadrupole, 2.97e-16) but is a single 2.3 sigma difference, not a refutation; (ii) A_E2 = 1.00 in later analyses (NOT READ) against 0.88; (iii) better Cs fountains and optical-optical ratios. Does any of it change the conclusion AS THE TREE USES IT? No, and this is computed rather than presumed: the tree uses the six coefficients and the two uncertainties, not the ratio value or the drift limits. A_E2 -> 1.00 moves the optical/optical eps_det by 1.7%; the Cs g-factor term (the dropped H-GCS) moves the optical/Cs eps_det by <= 1%; the source's alpha term the tree omits moves it by 2.2% under H1; the verdict EPS_NUCLEAR_OVER_DET (398, 114) and CS_CHANNEL_COARSER_BY's order (2 vs 100) do not move. M's hypothesis therefore finds, for this result, later data that sharpen it (a 2.3 sigma shift in the ratio value, a revised A_E2, a named ~1% Cs term) but none that moves what the tree rests on it. Evidence against the hypothesis here: the tree-relevant coefficients are ratios of derivatives whose leading parts (B = 0, -1; A_Cs integer 2) are exact power-law counting reproduced by the tree's own CONTROL 1 and by the Casimir estimate.
grade_evidence: The READ values stand verbatim: A_E3 = -5.95, A_E2 = 0.88, A_Cs = 2.83, B_E3 = B_E2 = 0, B_Cs = -1, 3e-16 and 6e-16 are all printed on pp.1 and 4 of 1407.0164v2, the tree's dict equals them, and Table I/II arithmetic re-derives (rederive A-B, G). The grade is NARROWED, not STANDS, on the rule's 'a hypothesis the tree drops': the tree's quote at address.py:436-440 elides the source's condition for B_Cs = -1 (the Cs nuclear g-factor's negligible sensitivity to the strong interaction), which is the one condition a displaced vev directly violates by moving X_q; and its optical/Cs sensitivity (address.py:625-628) drops the source's alpha term under H1. The narrowing is QUANTIFIED here and is small: <= 1% (g_Cs, snippet-level exponent) and 2.2% (alpha term, computed), moving no tree verdict (EPS_NUCLEAR_OVER_DET 398/114). Two discrepancies recorded, neither a refutation: CS_CHANNEL_COARSER_BY = 2 is the quotient of one-digit roundings (1.72-1.84 from the table), and the tree's 'Cs-limited' is Cs-referenced statistics rather than Cs systematics. Not WRONG: nothing contradicts the source. Not DATA-DEPENDENT: the moved data (A_E2, the later ratio value) move no conclusion the tree draws.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree names H-GCS (g_I held fixed, 'negligible' strong-interaction sensitivity of the Cs g-factor) and the omitted (A_opt - A_Cs) K_alpha term as hypotheses at the eps_det sites, or includes them. To DATA-DEPENDENT: a READ current Cs kappa_q or A_E2 large enough to move eps_det by an order of magnitude (none suggested: ~1e-2 and ~1e-1 relative). To OPEN for the coefficients: nothing -- they are READ. Reading Lange 2021 / Huntemann 2014 at source (alphaXiv quota reset) would convert the A_E2 = 1.00 and ratio-value rows from NAMED-NOT-READ to READ without changing any computed consequence stated here.
